title: An H2 section should contain at least one file-list item

spec.name: llms.txt (llmstxt.org)
spec.normative_quote: Zero or more markdown sections delimited by H2 headers, containing "file lists" of URLs where further detail is available
spec.note: conformance_testable is false. This id is a warn, not a fail, on disk today (check-security-txt.mjs precedent for the analogous decision does not apply here -- llmstxt.org genuinely has no conformance concept for an empty H2 section, so warn stays warn; rule_class: convention permits either severity). Verified against a live fetch of https://llmstxt.org/ on 2026-07-30. Corrects a prior defect: the original quote was a close paraphrase, not the spec's own sentence.

applicability: An H2 section whose body is entirely empty -- AND ONLY IN A BODY WITH A VALID H1. The shared reference returns immediately when the first non-blank line is not an H1 ('structure is unrecoverable past this point'), so this rule never runs on an H1-less body however many empty H2 sections it contains. Added by the ADR 0036 Posture-3 rehearsal, which found this precondition unstated here and in llms-txt-non-link-list-item; it is the same omission ADR 0011's security.txt rehearsal found and fixed on that one rule only (cases/h2-under-missing-h1.txt below pins it).
expectation: SPEC VERSION 2 (llms-structure.mjs LLMS_STRUCTURE_SPEC_VERSION = 2). Every H2 section has at least one non-blank line under it, up to the next H2 or end of file. The line may be a list item, prose, or a sub-heading -- v2 asks only that the section is not DANGLING. A prose section ('## Expertise' followed by a paragraph) is legal, where v1 required a list item and flagged it. The title still reads true and the id is unchanged: an empty section has no file list, and nothing else either. Emission is per empty section: a body with three dangling H2 headings emits this finding three times.
policy_note: v2 DIVERGES from the normative quote above, deliberately. llmstxt.org describes H2 sections as containing 'file lists' of URLs; v2 permits a section that carries prose instead. The reason is content: the live index at https://jonathanlloyd.me/llms.txt has a '## Expertise' section that is one descriptive paragraph, and v1 reported it as a defect on every weekly run. The residual defect v2 still catches is the unambiguous one -- a heading an author left with nothing under it. Paired with the same-dated relaxation in llms-txt-non-link-list-item; both were prompted by the mantle-LifegamesPortal producer contract test.

cases.name: an H2 section under a missing H1 is NOT reported -- the validator returns early (ADR 0036: pins the unstated precondition)
an H2 section with prose but no list is legal (v2: pins the relaxation)
a dangling H2 heading with nothing at all under it
